title: NotebookLM or a study app for exams?
summary: Keep NotebookLM if your main question is what your assigned sources say.
body_markdown:
Keep NotebookLM if your main question is what your assigned sources say. Try a dedicated study app if your bottleneck is returning to missed material and explaining an answer with the notes closed.


Educato publishes this page and makes one of the apps on it. We list it where it fits, with its limits.

## Should I use NotebookLM or a study app to examine a course source?


Choose NotebookLM when the answer depends on finding the right passage in a reading, slide deck or handout. Choose a practice app when you can find the passage easily but keep making the same mistake a week later. A single question from an introductory statistics course shows how to tell those problems apart, even when the wrong answer sounds almost exactly like the lecture.


### One campus survey, two defensible percentages


Imagine a professor gives you two pages about a fictional campus bus survey. The methods handout says that 200 students received invitations and 80 returned questionnaires. A slide says that 60 respondents wanted a later bus. The exam question asks, “What share of respondents wanted a later bus, and what can the survey tell us about everyone invited?” Before making cards, write down your fraction and finish the sentence “This fraction describes…”


A weak answer says, “Seventy-five percent of students wanted a later bus.” The arithmetic works. The noun at the end quietly extends the finding to a group the survey never heard from in full. A stronger answer says, “Sixty of the 80 respondents wanted a later bus, or 75%. Among all 200 invitees, 60 people explicitly supported it. We have no answer from the 120 who did not return the questionnaire.”


What about a classmate who gets 30%? Ask them to write their question above their calculation. “What percentage of invitees returned a questionnaire supporting a later bus?” has a perfectly good answer of 60 divided by 200, or 30%. “What percentage of invitees wanted a later bus?” remains open. Counting someone as having sent no reply is different from counting them as opposed. A good practice session should let you explain why both numbers can be correct and still answer different questions.


### Is NotebookLM good for exams?


Yes, especially when exam questions draw on several assigned sources. In the survey example, put the methods handout and results slide in the same notebook. Ask “Which document gives the number invited, and which gives the count supporting the proposal? Quote the label beside each count.” Open the originals and check the labels. If the slide only says “60 in favor,” the methods page supplies the context you need to interpret it.


NotebookLM can make flashcards, slide decks and audio or video overviews from sources. Its mobile app supports offline listening to downloaded Audio Overviews. On a commute, pause after the description of the survey and say aloud whose preferences are missing. Later, cover the slide and reconstruct both fractions. If listening brings back the story but you still divide by 200 whenever you see the word “students,” you have identified a specific question worth practicing again.[Read the product details](https://support.google.com/gemininotebook/answer/16213268?hl=en) .


### Which NotebookLM alternatives help with repeated mistakes?


Knowt fits a student who wants a small set of questions to return to through spaced repetition. Write two cards with the same numbers. Give the first the prompt “Among returned questionnaires, what fraction supported the proposal?” Give the second “Among invitations sent, what fraction produced a reply in support?” Put the fraction and its units on each reverse side. A card that simply asks “What was the survey percentage?” is impossible to grade fairly.


For the next review, change the number of invitations to 240 while keeping the number of replies and supporters fixed. Before calculating, predict which percentage must stay the same. The fraction among respondents still uses 80 as its denominator. The fraction of invitations yielding a supportive reply falls to one quarter. Getting the prediction right gives you a better reason to retire the card than recognizing “75%” on sight.


Knowt lets you create or import cards and offers free Learn Mode. Student Ultra adds summaries of PDFs, presentations and lecture recordings and can generate study podcasts. If your two survey cards are already written, you can try reviewing them before deciding whether converting a semester of recordings would justify a paid plan.[Read the product details](https://knowt.com/plans?tab=Student+Ultra) .


### Educato vs NotebookLM: which should I choose to practice a written answer?


Choose NotebookLM to examine what a source actually says and Educato to practice producing a written answer before seeing feedback. **Educato is best for** practicing written explanations from a mix of PDFs, presentations and photos of notes. Use the survey slide and your handwritten correction to attempt an open answer. Try a question with no calculation at all. “The transit committee says the survey establishes majority support among invitees. What would you need to know to assess that claim?” Check whether your answer explains how the missing replies could change the conclusion.


For instance, if every missing student opposed the change, the 60 known supporters would be a minority of the 200 invited. If all 120 missing students supported it, supporters would number 180. Both possibilities fit the returned questionnaires. That pair of examples gives you something concrete to look for when reading feedback on your paragraph. **Limits.** Full Educato access is paid, including live voice. For this written task, the important feature is the chance to produce the explanation from scratch.


### Is NotebookLM worth it?


A personal Gmail account allows 100 notebooks with up to 50 sources per notebook, excluding notes from the source count. Google AI Plus and Pro raise those limits. If the methods and results for one unit fit comfortably together, a higher cap buys no advantage on this question. A course with dozens of readings that must be compared in the same notebook presents a different reason to consider the Google AI bundle.


There is a practical cost to splitting the survey across two tools. A copied card can outlive the slide it came from. Write the source title and the original group label on the answer side before you change the numbers for practice. That way, when your practice deck says 240 and the lecture says 200, you can tell which figure belongs in an answer about the assigned survey.


Before choosing an app for the rest of the term, take a clean sheet of paper and answer a parallel question about a dining hall poll. If you need the original slide to remember what “respondents” means, keep working with the sources. If you can define the term but lose track of it halfway through a calculation, bring back the paired cards. If both fractions come easily and the committee’s claim still stumps you, spend the next session writing the missing explanation.
